records.issue_text: [BUG] Reordering initWatcher to run after search.init means events written between snapshot query and watcher start are silently dropped from the search index. A dashboard saved during the (potentially minutes-long) index build is missed by the watcher and absent from the snapshot query that ran before it, leaving the search index permanently stale for that resource until a full rebuild; the old order (watcher first) captured those events.

records.issue_text: [BUG] Dropping the cacheMu lock held across BuildIndex allows two concurrent callers of getOrCreateIndex for the same NamespacedResource to both build and register an index, with the last writer to b.cache[key] winning and the loser's file-based bleve index (opened on disk under opts.Root) leaked. Concurrent first-time access to the same resource type opens two bleve indices on the same directory; the loser's index handle is dropped without Close, leaking file handles and, on file-backed indexes, leaving two writers to the same dir; also the caller that receives the orphaned index serves a stale index that never receives cache updates from subsequent builds.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] History and Origin call s.search.History/Origin with no nil check, and previously their per-method Init guaranteed the search support was initialized before use; after moving Init to construction, any server constructed without search configured (s.search == nil — a supported configuration, as Search itself checks for it) panics with nil pointer dereference on History/Origin. A deployment with search disabled that issues a History or Origin RPC crashes the handler with a nil-pointer panic instead of returning the error the old Init-guarded path produced.

records.issue_text: [BUG] Removing the per-request Init(ctx) checks means that when background initialization fails (s.initErr set inside Init's goroutine), every RPC handler — Read, List, Search, Watch, History, Create, Update, Delete — now executes against an uninitialized server instead of returning the init error. A transient DB failure during index build permanently poisons the server via the cached initErr, but callers no longer see it: they get silently wrong/empty results (no watcher running, no search index, List serving raw backend state) rather than the error the old contract promised.
records.rationale: The diff shows init errors are now surfaced at construction time, not hidden from callers: `NewResourceServer` explicitly calls `err := s.Init(ctx)` and on failure does `return nil, err`. Therefore, if `Init` sets `s.initErr` during initialization, the server will not be returned/registered and RPC handlers won’t run “against an uninitialized server”. Also, the finding’s claim that `s.initErr` is set “inside Init’s goroutine” is not supported by the shown `Init` changes (the snippet shows synchronous init steps, just reordered), so the described mechanism isn’t verifiable from this diff.

records.issue_text: [BUG] Reordering so search index build runs before initWatcher means write events that occur during the (potentially long) index build are never delivered to the search index. Previously the watcher was started first so events during build were consumed; now any Create/Update/Delete landing between the DB snapshot used by build and initWatcher's start is permanently missing from the index until that resource is written again — stale search results with no error anywhere.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Removing the BuildIndex-wide cacheMu lock allows two concurrent index builds for the same NamespacedResource to both create a bleve index at the same on-disk directory filepath.Join(b.opts.Root, key.Namespace, fmt.Sprintf("%s.%s", key.Resource, key.Group)). Concurrent builders for the same key race writing the same bleve directory (file corruption / index opening errors) and the later b.cache[key] = idx last-write-wins discards one builder's resource-version bookkeeping; previously the whole-function lock serialized builds. Whoever gets bitten: any path that triggers two simultaneous cold-start builds of the same resource type — now more likely since server.go's Init moved into construction while other entrypoints (getOrCreateIndex on cache miss) can still race a slow build.

records.issue_text: [BUG] Removing the cacheMu lock for the duration of BuildIndex allows concurrent builds of the same key to run in parallel, with two bleve.New(dir) calls targeting the same on-disk directory. Two requests that miss the cache for the same NamespacedResource simultaneously both construct an index at the same filepath (bleve.New on the same dir), corrupting or failing one of the on-disk indexes; the cache then does last-write-wins, so the surviving in-memory index may reference the corrupted directory. Previously the full-build lock serialized this.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] With the Init call removed from History and Origin, these methods dereference s.search with no nil guard, while Search retains an explicit 'search index not configured' check.
